4th Period.workingNow: Using class and ID selectors to target specific parts of your page with different styles.
4th Period.weeklyDeliverable: Your About Me page with an external CSS stylesheet linked — custom fonts/colors, class/ID selectors, padding/margin, and an organized layout — pushed and ready to submit Sunday night.
4th Period.smartGoal: I can write class and ID selectors so that I can style specific elements differently from the rest of my page.
4th Period.contentStandard: CA CS Standards 6-8.AP.13 — Create prototypes using structured code, organized into separate linked pages, to fulfill a design requirement.
4th Period.eldStandard: ELD.PI.6-8.1 — Exchanging information and ideas with others through collaborative discussions.
agenda: I do: model a class selector and an ID selector (8 min)
We do: style one shared element together (6 min)
You do: add a class or ID to two elements and style them (25 min)
Exit Ticket: what's one difference between a class and an ID? (6 min)
4th Period.connections: Yesterday you linked a stylesheet and changed simple defaults. Today you get more precise — targeting specific parts of your page instead of styling everything the same way. Tomorrow we look at spacing.

6th Period.workingNow: Assigning group roles, then designing your main character and its states.
6th Period.weeklyDeliverable: A group platformer game plan (character states, at least one obstacle/enemy state, and a labeled level sketch) created in groups of four.
6th Period.smartGoal: I can design my character's states so that my group's platformer has a clear state machine at its center.
6th Period.contentStandard: CA CS Standards 6-8.AP.10 — Use flowcharts and/or pseudocode to design solutions to complex problems.
6th Period.eldStandard: ELD.PI.6-8.1 — Exchanging information and ideas with others through collaborative discussions.
agenda: Assign group roles: Character Lead, State Machine Lead, Level Lead, Notes Lead (5 min)
I do: model a platformer character's states (idle/walk/jump) (7 min)
You do: as a group, design your character and its states (28 min)
Exit Ticket: list your character's states so far (5 min)
6th Period.connections: Yesterday your group picked a game idea. Today you get specific — designing the main character and mapping out its states, the same state machine thinking you used in Sprite Lab, just bigger and more creative.
